title: Deep Dive: Chase Sapphire Preferred's 100,000 Point Windfall – A Limited-Time Travel Game Changer
imageAlt: Chase Sapphire Preferred card with a backdrop of travel destinations
author: Dilan Madushanka
snippet: A landmark opportunity in the travel rewards sphere is rapidly approaching its conclusion. The Chase Sapphire Preferred® Card is currently presenting an extraordinary 100,000 Ultimate Rewards® bonus points...
content:
A landmark opportunity in the travel rewards sphere is rapidly approaching its conclusion. The Chase Sapphire Preferred® Card is currently presenting an extraordinary 100,000 Ultimate Rewards® bonus points, a promotion with the potential to significantly reshape your travel horizons. However, this exceptional offer is ephemeral, set to expire precisely at 9 AM EST on May 15, 2025. This comprehensive analysis explores the substantial value, strategic considerations, and the sheer travel empowerment embedded within this fleeting chance.

For both seasoned globetrotters and astute consumers, the Chase Sapphire Preferred® Card has long been recognized as a vital component of an effective rewards strategy. Its combination of adaptable points, valuable travel safeguards, and a justifiable annual fee has solidified its position as a consistent favorite. The current 100,000-point welcome bonus, however, elevates the card from merely "great" to a "must-consider," albeit for a limited period. This is more than just a standard sign-up incentive; it represents a significant travel fund, a golden opportunity for those who act with foresight and timeliness.

The infrequency of such a generous offer cannot be emphasized enough. The Chase Sapphire Preferred® Card last featured a 100,000-point sign-up bonus in 2021, making its current reappearance a noteworthy event in the competitive travel rewards market. High-value offers of this magnitude are typically strategic initiatives by card issuers, aimed at attracting a substantial influx of new cardholders. For consumers, this translates to a rare occasion to acquire a premium travel currency at an unusually accelerated pace.

This article will meticulously examine every aspect of this offer: the intrinsic value of these 100,000 points, the card's ongoing benefits that extend well beyond this initial bonus, the demographics that stand to gain the most, and the critical importance of the May 15th deadline. If your ambition is to significantly enhance your travel capabilities, a thorough understanding of this Chase Sapphire Preferred® offer is the foundational and most crucial step.

The Offer Deconstructed: Essential Details

The core of this widespread interest is a simple yet remarkably powerful proposition. New cardholders of the Chase Sapphire Preferred® Card have the opportunity to earn 100,000 bonus Ultimate Rewards® points. To access this significant points cache, a new cardholder is required to spend $5,000 on purchases within the first three months of account opening.

The card is associated with a $95 annual fee, a figure that appears modest when compared to the immediate and sustained value it delivers, particularly with this amplified bonus.

The most pivotal detail, however, is the unwavering deadline: this offer will terminate at 9 AM EST on May 15, 2025. This is not a vaguely defined "limited-time offer"; it is a definitive cutoff. Missing this window means forfeiting the 100,000 points. This precise deadline instills a potent sense of urgency, a well-established marketing tactic that often signals the conclusion of an unusually generous promotional phase. For Chase, this is likely a strategic move to boost second-quarter acquisition numbers for one of its premier products. For consumers, it is an unambiguous call to prompt action.

The $5,000 spending threshold within a three-month timeframe averages to roughly $1,667 per month. While this represents a notable sum, it is often attainable for many households by strategically aligning larger planned expenditures or by redirecting regular spending onto the new card. The key insight here is that the pathway to acquiring 100,000 points is clearly demarcated.

The reappearance of this offer after a several-year absence indicates that it is not a standard, recurring promotion. It is a special occurrence, and its conclusion may well signal a reversion to a lower, more typical welcome bonus for the Sapphire Preferred. Consequently, the "last chance" messaging frequently associated with such offers carries substantial weight.

Unpacking the Value: The True Worth of 100,000 Points

The phrase "100,000 points" possesses an inherent appeal, but its genuine value is rooted in its flexibility and redemption potency within the Chase Ultimate Rewards® program. This is not merely a numerical figure; it is a significant travel asset offering multiple avenues to realize substantial worth.

Baseline Value: Travel Portal and Cash Back

At a fundamental level, these 100,000 points equate to $1,000 if redeemed for cash back (at a rate of 1 cent per point). However, the value proposition markedly improves when these points are applied towards travel. When redeeming points for airfare, hotels, car rentals, and cruises through the Chase Travel℠ portal, cardholders receive a 25% bonus in value. This elevates the worth of each point to 1.25 cents, thereby making the 100,000-point bonus equivalent to $1,250 for travel booked via the portal. This 25% enhancement is a core characteristic of the Sapphire Preferred and a significant distinguishing feature. For many, this direct $1,250 in travel value is, in itself, a persuasive reason to acquire the card.

Enhanced Value: The Power of Transfer Partners

The true potential, and where astute travelers often extract even greater returns, is found in Chase's network of airline and hotel transfer partners. Chase Ultimate Rewards® points can be transferred on a 1:1 basis to a variety of popular loyalty programs. This transferability is what elevates the Chase Sapphire Preferred® from a good travel card to an exceptional one, and the 100,000-point bonus provides a substantial initial balance to explore these high-value redemption avenues. For example, transferring 100,000 points to World of Hyatt® could secure multiple nights at premium properties, potentially yielding a value far exceeding the 1.25 cents per point portal redemption. NerdWallet values Hyatt points around 2.2 cents each, theoretically making 100,000 points worth $2,200 when transferred and redeemed strategically. Similarly, transferring points to airline partners like Air France-KLM Flying Blue or Virgin Atlantic can unlock business or first-class international flights, often providing an outsized value per point, sometimes reaching 3, 4, or even more cents per point.

Current Transfer Bonus Opportunities:

Adding another layer of potential value, Chase frequently offers limited-time transfer bonuses to specific partners. As of early May 2025, cardholders can benefit from a 25% bonus when transferring points to Air France-KLM Flying Blue (valid through May 31, 2025) and a similar 25% bonus for transfers to Virgin Atlantic Flying Club (extending through June 15, 2025). Leveraging such a promotion means your 100,000 Ultimate Rewards® points could transform into 125,000 airline miles, further amplifying their redemption power.

In essence, the 100,000-point bonus from the Chase Sapphire Preferred® is a flexible asset that can unlock anywhere from $1,000 in cash to potentially several thousands of dollars in luxury travel, contingent on the redemption strategy employed.

Beyond the Bonus: Enduring Value of the Sapphire Preferred

While the 100,000-point welcome offer is the immediate draw, the Chase Sapphire Preferred® Card provides a compelling array of ongoing benefits that deliver lasting value long after the initial bonus has been utilized. These features contribute to its $95 annual fee being widely considered a sound investment.

Robust Rewards Earning Structure:

The card excels in rewarding common spending, particularly travel and dining: 5x points on travel via Chase Travel℠, 3x on dining worldwide (including takeout/delivery), 3x on select streaming services, 3x on online grocery purchases (exclusions apply), 2x on other travel, and 1x on all other purchases. This structure allows for accelerated point accumulation.

$50 Annual Chase Travel Hotel Credit:

Each anniversary year, cardholders receive a $50 statement credit for hotel stays purchased through Chase Travel℠, effectively reducing the annual fee to $45 for those who use it.

Comprehensive Travel Protections:

The Sapphire Preferred is known for its strong travel insurance benefits:

  • Primary Auto Rental Collision Damage Waiver: A standout benefit offering primary coverage for theft and collision damage on rental cars paid for with the card.
  • Trip Cancellation/Interruption Insurance: Reimbursement for prepaid, non-refundable travel expenses up to $10,000 per person and $20,000 per trip for covered reasons.
  • Baggage Delay Insurance & Lost Luggage Reimbursement: Coverage for essential purchases due to baggage delays and reimbursement for lost or damaged luggage.
  • Trip Delay Reimbursement: Coverage for expenses like meals and lodging if travel is significantly delayed.

Purchase Protection and Extended Warranty:

The card also offers protection for new purchases against damage or theft and extends U.S. manufacturer's warranties.

These ongoing benefits underscore that the Chase Sapphire Preferred® is a well-rounded travel companion, making its annual fee justifiable for many, independent of the initial bonus.

Strategic Implications: Timing and Tactics

The Chase Sapphire Preferred's 100,000-point offer is a significant event requiring strategic consideration from potential applicants.

The Power of Urgency:

The May 15, 2025, 9 AM EST deadline is paramount. This "last chance" framing motivates action. The offer's previous appearance in 2021 reinforces its special nature.

Meeting the Minimum Spending Requirement ($5,000 in 3 Months):

Strategic planning is key to meeting the $5,000 spend. Applicants should assess upcoming large purchases, shift regular spending (groceries, gas, utilities), and consider prepaying bills where feasible, all while avoiding unnecessary debt.

Chase's Market Positioning:

This offer is a strategic move by Chase to attract new customers in a competitive market. The defined offer period allows for a concentrated marketing effort. Its conclusion may signal a shift in Chase's acquisition strategy for this card.

For consumers, the implication is clear: evaluate your finances and travel goals promptly. If the Sapphire Preferred aligns with your needs and you can responsibly meet the spend, the window to secure 100,000 bonus points is closing.

The Engine Room: Understanding the Chase Ultimate Rewards® Ecosystem

The 100,000 bonus points are your entry, but the Chase Ultimate Rewards® program is the engine driving their value.

Unmatched Flexibility:

Ultimate Rewards® points are versatile, usable through the Chase Travel℠ portal (with a 25% value boost), transferable 1:1 to numerous airline and hotel partners, or redeemable for cash back, gift cards, or merchandise (though travel redemptions usually offer better value).

High-Value Transfer Partners:

Chase partners with leading loyalty programs, including airlines like United MileagePlus®, Southwest Rapid Rewards®, Air France-KLM Flying Blue, and Virgin Atlantic Flying Club, and hotel programs like World of Hyatt®, Marriott Bonvoy®, and IHG Rewards Club. World of Hyatt is particularly lauded for high redemption values.

Leveraging Transfer Bonuses:

Periodic transfer bonuses, like the current 25% bonuses to Flying Blue (ends May 31, 2025) and Virgin Atlantic (ends June 15, 2025), can further enhance point value.

Pooling Points:

Points from other Chase Ultimate Rewards®-earning cards can be pooled with the Sapphire Preferred, unlocking their full transfer potential.

The Ultimate Rewards® program is a comprehensive travel platform, and the 100,000-point bonus provides a substantial foundation to leverage this powerful ecosystem.

Who Stands to Benefit Most from This Offer?

The Chase Sapphire Preferred®, with its current 100,000-point offer, appeals broadly, but certain individuals are especially well-positioned to maximize its value.

Travel Rewards Beginners:

Often recommended as a first travel rewards card, its straightforward earning, 25% portal bonus, and reasonable $95 annual fee are less daunting than ultra-premium alternatives. The 100,000-point bonus offers an immediate, tangible demonstration of travel rewards' power.

Experienced Points and Miles Enthusiasts:

Seasoned users value the flexibility of Ultimate Rewards® and access to high-value transfer partners. The 100,000 points can be strategically used for aspirational awards like international premium cabin flights or luxury hotel stays.

Value-Conscious Travelers:

Those prioritizing maximum value will appreciate the multiple redemption avenues, from the $1,250 portal value to potentially higher returns via partner transfers. The $50 annual hotel credit further enhances affordability.

Those Planning Significant Upcoming Travel:

This offer can substantially boost a travel budget, covering flights, accommodations, or activities, making planned trips more affordable or enabling upgrades.

Individuals Who Can Comfortably Meet the Minimum Spend:

The $5,000 spend in three months is a key qualifier. Those who can meet this through regular and planned purchases without incurring debt are ideal.

People Who Value Flexibility:

The adaptability of Ultimate Rewards® means points aren't tied to a single program, offering options if travel plans or program values change.

Considerations for Chase's 5/24 Rule:

Applicants should be mindful of Chase's unwritten "5/24 rule" (generally, denial if you've opened five or more credit cards from any bank in the past 24 months). This high-value offer might be a priority for those nearing this limit.

The decision to apply should stem from a careful assessment of personal spending, travel goals, and financial health. For many, this offer is exceptionally attractive if it aligns with responsible financial practices.

A Brief Look at the Competitive Landscape

While this analysis centers on the Chase Sapphire Preferred's 100,000-point offer, acknowledging the competitive environment highlights its compelling nature. May 2025 has seen several issuers vying for consumer attention.

A notable competing offer, also nearing its end, is from the Capital One Venture Rewards Credit Card. It has featured 75,000 bonus miles after a $4,000 spend in three months, plus a one-time $250 Capital One Travel credit for the first year. This offer, valued around $1,000 in travel, has an earlier deadline, typically May 12th or 13th, 2025. The Capital One Venture card, also with a $95 annual fee, is known for its simple 2x miles on every purchase.

Comparing the two:

  • Chase Sapphire Preferred®: 100,000 points ($1,250+ value) for $5,000 spend. Deadline: May 15th.
  • Capital One Venture Rewards: 75,000 miles + $250 credit ($1,000 value) for $4,000 spend. Deadline: May 12th/13th.

While both are strong, the Sapphire Preferred's 100,000 points offer a potentially higher redemption ceiling via Ultimate Rewards® transfer partners. Other cards, like The Platinum Card® from American Express and Marriott Bonvoy Amex offers, also contribute to a competitive market. However, for a versatile travel card with a sub-$100 annual fee, the Sapphire Preferred's current bonus is exceptionally competitive.

Conclusion: Seize the Moment – 100,000 Reasons to Act Fast

The Chase Sapphire Preferred® Card's 100,000 Ultimate Rewards® bonus points offer is a significant opportunity for travelers to inject immense value into their future journeys. With a redemption value of at least $1,250 via Chase Travel℠ and potentially much more through transfer partners, this bonus is one of the most compelling in recent times.

The card itself is a robust travel tool, offering strong ongoing rewards, a $50 annual hotel credit, and comprehensive travel protections, including primary auto rental insurance, justifying its $95 annual fee.

However, the window to capitalize on this 100,000-point offer is narrow: the deadline is 9 AM EST on May 15, 2025. The rarity of this offer, last seen in 2021, suggests it won't linger.

For potential applicants, the call to action is direct: evaluate your spending and travel goals, check your eligibility (including Chase's 5/24 rule), and if the card fits, act decisively before the May 15th deadline. In a dynamic rewards landscape, moments of extraordinary value like this are to be seized.

title: United's New Card Lineup: More Perks, Higher Fees – What's the Real Deal for Your Wallet?
imageAlt: New United Airlines co-branded credit cards
author: News Contributor
snippet: United and Chase have refreshed their co-branded card lineup with new benefits, different ways to earn elite status points (PQPs), and increased annual fees for most cards.
content:
Hey fellow travelers! If you've got a United Airlines credit card from Chase, or if you've been eyeing one, listen up. United and Chase rolled out a significant refresh to their co-branded card family back in March 2025.1 We're talking new benefits, different ways to earn those coveted elite status points (PQPs), and yes, for most of these cards, a bump in the annual fee.2 The new perks kicked in right away, but if you're an existing cardholder, you'll see those higher fees on your renewal date on or after August 1, 2025 (or a bit later, January 1, 2026, if you have the United Explorer card).3

Now, this isn't just United shaking things up for fun. It feels like a broader trend where credit card companies are trying to pack in more value – or at least, what they hope feels like more value – to justify those higher price tags. United’s talking about "unmatched value," with some cards supposedly offering benefits that add up to hundreds, even over a thousand dollars a year.4 But here’s the thing: these cards are definitely leaning into what folks are calling the "coupon book" style.6 Think lots of little credits for specific things, which means you, the traveler, have to be a bit more strategic to make sure you’re actually getting your money's worth.

So, the big question for us U.S. travelers is: are these revamped United cards a smart move for our wallets, or just a more complicated way to fly? Let's dig in.

What’s the Big Deal? A Quick Look at the Changes

The main shift here is that these cards are trying to be more than just a way to earn miles and get a free checked bag. They've woven in a whole bunch of statement credits for services you might use, like rideshares to the airport, Instacart for groceries (a bit random for a travel card, but okay!), and even for booking hotels through specific United portals.1

This means you can't just set it and forget it. To really get the value, you’ll need to be more of an active manager of your card benefits. And let's be real, if you don't use those specific services, or if you forget to jump through the hoops to get the credits, that "value" disappears pretty quickly.6

Zooming In on the Cards: What’s New for You?

Let's break down what’s changed for some of the most popular United cards.

The United℠ Explorer Card: Still Your Go-To for a Few Trips a Year?

This card has always been a solid pick for folks who fly United occasionally.

The Fee: It’s $0 for the first year, then $150. That’s up from the old $95 (after the first year).9

New Perks to Note:

  • A $100 United Travel Credit if you spend $10,000 on the card in a year (this comes as TravelBank cash, which has some rules).8
  • A 10,000-mile discount on an award flight if you spend $20,000 in a year.10
  • Credits for United Hotels (up to $100 a year), rideshares (up to $60 a year), and Instacart (up to $120 a year).11

Chasing Status (PQP): You’ll earn 1 Premier Qualifying Point (PQP) for every $20 you spend, capped at 1,000 PQPs a year.6 It’s a small boost if you’re aiming for United Premier status.

Heads Up on Changes:

  • Those two United Club one-time passes are still around, but now you (or an authorized user) actually have to be there to use them. So, gifting them just got trickier.7
  • If you have elite status, the perk of getting Premier upgrades on award tickets is going away after August 1, 2025.14 That’s a bummer for some.

The United Quest℠ Card: Stepping Up Your United Game?

For more frequent United flyers, the Quest card got a refresh too.

The Fee: Now $350, up from $250.14

New/Improved Goodies:

  • The annual United purchase credit is now $200, but it’s TravelBank cash (which expires in a year) instead of a more flexible statement credit.6
  • You get one 10,000-mile award flight discount each year, and can earn a second one if you spend $20,000.14
  • Credits for Renowned Hotels & Resorts (up to $150), rideshares (up to $100), and Instacart (up to $180).14

Serious PQP Power: You get a 1,000 PQP bonus each year (starting in 2026) and can earn up to 18,000 PQPs from spending (1 PQP per $20 spent).16 This is a significant jump if status is your aim.

The United Club℠ Infinite Card: For the Ultimate United Loyalist?

This is United's top-tier personal card, and it saw the biggest fee increase.

The Fee: A hefty $695, up from $525.17

Premium Perks:

  • You can earn up to two 10,000-mile award flight discounts a year (each needs $20,000 in spending).14
  • Credits for Renowned Hotels & Resorts (up to $200), rideshares (up to $150), and a complimentary Instacart+ membership plus up to $240 in Instacart credits.17

Top-Tier PQP Earning: A 1,500 PQP bonus annually (from 2026), a faster earn rate of 1 PQP for every $15 spent, and a huge annual cap of 28,000 PQPs.16

United Club Access Nuances: You still get your United Club membership. But, if you want the "All Access Membership" (which gets you into Star Alliance partner lounges and lets you bring two guests instead of one), you now need Premier Gold status or higher, or you have to spend a cool $50,000 on the card each year.17

A Quick Mention for Business Travelers: The United℠ Business Card

This card also saw its fee go up to $150 (after the first year, which is $0) from $99.20 It gained some similar credits for TravelBank cash, hotels, rideshares, and Instacart, plus a boosted PQP earning cap of 4,000 PQPs a year.20

The Upsides: Where These Cards Might Still Make Sense

If you're laser-focused on climbing the United Premier status ladder, the beefed-up PQP earning on these cards is genuinely attractive, especially since United is making status harder to get in 2025.16 The Club Infinite and Quest cards, in particular, can give you a serious leg up.16

And those new statement credits? They can save you real cash, but the big "if" is whether they match how you already spend your money. If you’re an Instacart devotee or always take an Uber to the airport, then great, you’ll likely see some benefit.21

The Downsides: Navigating the "Coupon Book"

Here’s where it gets tricky. The sheer number and complexity of these credits can be a headache.6 Many aren't automatic – you might need to enroll, or they’re doled out in small monthly chunks that don’t roll over.6 If you’re not diligent, it’s easy to miss out on using them, and then that "value" is just theoretical.6

Using the hotel credits often means booking through United's specific hotel portals, which might not always have the best prices or could prevent you from earning hotel loyalty points or using your existing hotel elite perks.7

Plus, some old reliable perks have been watered down, like the Explorer card’s Club passes being harder to gift 7 or the Quest card’s travel credit becoming less flexible TravelBank cash.6

Making Them Work for You (If You Decide To)

If you’re a die-hard United fan and one of these cards still calls to you, here’s the game plan:

PQP Strategy: If status is your main goal, focus your spending on your United card. But do the math – it takes a LOT of spending to hit high PQP levels this way.16

Credit Conquest: Get organized! Set reminders for monthly credits. Understand the fine print for each one. For hotel credits, always compare prices before booking through United’s portals.6

These cards now seem best for:

  • Explorer: Occasional United flyers who value bags/boarding and can use enough credits to make the $150 fee worth it.9
  • Quest: Frequent United flyers chasing status who can maximize the TravelBank cash and other credits to justify $350.25
  • Club Infinite: The ultimate United loyalist who lives in the lounge, aims for top status via massive spend, and can juggle all the premium credits to make the $695 fee pay off.27

What About Other Travel Cards?

It’s worth remembering that cards like the Chase Sapphire Preferred® are still out there. You can transfer its points 1:1 to United 3, it often has huge welcome offers (like the recent 100,000 points) 29, earns well on general travel and dining 3, and has a simpler $95 annual fee. For many, the flexibility and straightforward value of a card like this might outweigh the complicated perks of the new United lineup.

So, What's the Verdict for Your Wallet?

This United card refresh is a mixed bag. More potential value? Sure, if you’re willing to work for it.4 But it comes with higher fees and a lot more mental gymnastics.7

Before you apply or decide to keep your current United card, ask yourself:

  • Will I really use these specific credits without changing how I normally spend?
  • How loyal am I really to United?
  • Could a simpler, more flexible travel card be a better fit for me?

The days of United cards being a simple choice are probably over. They now require a good, hard look to see if they match your travel style and how much effort you want to put into managing your rewards. Choose wisely, and happy travels!

title: Southwest Airlines' Transformation: A Traveler's Guide to New Fares & Perks
imageAlt: Illustration of Southwest Airlines new fare structure and benefits
author: Dilan Madushanka
snippet: Southwest Airlines is undergoing a significant overhaul, including a new fare system, assigned seating, and enhanced benefits for credit cardholders and elite status members, with changes rolling out from March 2025.
content:
Southwest Airlines, long known for its customer-friendly policies like "bags fly free" and open seating, is undergoing a significant overhaul. This transformation includes a new fare system, the introduction of assigned seating, and enhanced benefits for credit cardholders and elite status members.1 The airline aims to offer a wider range of travel experiences, with changes rolling out in phases starting March 2025 and continuing throughout the year.1

Decoding Southwest's New Fare Structure

Southwest is introducing four new fare types, replacing its familiar offerings. The Basic fare (formerly Wanna Get Away) launched on May 28, 2025, while Choice (formerly Wanna Get Away Plus), Choice Preferred (formerly Anytime), and Choice Extra (formerly Business Select) will be available in the third quarter of 2025, coinciding with the sale of assigned seating for flights in 2026.1

Key Features of the New Fares:

  • Basic (Formerly Wanna Get Away):
    • Seat Selection: Standard seat in the back, assigned at check-in.5
    • Boarding: Last group.4
    • Bags: Fees apply for checked bags.1
    • Changes/Cancellations: Non-refundable and non-changeable. Flight credits expire six months from the original booking date.4
    • Rapid Rewards: Lowest earning rate.3
  • Choice (Formerly Wanna Get Away Plus):
    • Seat Selection: Select a standard seat in the back at booking.5
    • Boarding: General group.5
    • Bags: Fees apply for checked bags.1
    • Changes/Cancellations: Transferable Flight Credit™ upon cancellation; free same-day confirmed changes (taxes/fees may apply).7
    • Rapid Rewards: Previously 6 points per dollar, adjusted in March 2025.3
  • Choice Preferred (Formerly Anytime):
    • Seat Selection: Select a preferred seat (front of cabin) or standard seat at booking.5
    • Boarding: Early general group.5
    • Bags: Fees apply for checked bags.1
    • Changes/Cancellations: Refundable; free same-day confirmed changes (taxes/fees may apply).4
    • Rapid Rewards: Previously 10 points per dollar.12
  • Choice Extra (Formerly Business Select):
    • Seat Selection: Select an Extra Legroom seat or any other seat at booking.5
    • Boarding: Priority (A1-A15).5
    • Bags: Two free checked bags included.1
    • Changes/Cancellations: Refundable; free same-day confirmed changes (taxes/fees may apply).12
    • Rapid Rewards: Highest earning rate; includes free Inflight Internet and a premium drink.3

"Bags Fly Free" Evolves (Effective May 28, 2025)

The "Bags Fly Free" policy is changing. For flights booked on or after May 28, 2025, bag fees will apply to Basic, Choice, and Choice Preferred fares.1 However:

  • Choice Extra fares still include two free checked bags.1
  • Southwest Rapid Rewards Credit Cardmembers get their first checked bag free (plus up to eight companions on the same reservation).1
  • A-List members get their first checked bag free (plus up to eight companions).5
  • A-List Preferred members get two free checked bags (plus up to eight companions).5

Carry-on bags (one standard, one personal) remain free for all.1

Flight Credits & Same-Day Travel Updates (Effective May 28, 2025)

  • Flight Credits: Credits from bookings made before May 28, 2025, do not expire if the original booking was made under terms that allowed for non-expiring credits and the cancellation also occurs before May 28, 2025. However, if a flight booked before May 27th is cancelled after May 28th, the resulting credit will expire.8 For credits from bookings/changes on or after May 28, 2025:
    • Basic fare credits expire six months from the original booking date.8
    • Choice, Choice Preferred, and Choice Extra credits are valid for travel completed within 12 months of the original ticket purchase date.8
    • Higher-tier fares offer Transferable Flight Credits™.11
  • Same-Day Change: Free for Choice Extra, Choice Preferred, and Choice fares. A-List/A-List Preferred members no longer get free same-day changes on Basic fares; they must purchase a qualifying higher fare.13
  • Same-Day Standby: Available for all fare types. A-List/A-List Preferred members still qualify for same-day standby on Basic fares.12

Enhanced Perks for Southwest Credit Cardholders

Southwest Rapid Rewards credit cards (issued by Chase) are gaining significant new benefits 1:

  • Seat Selection: Cardmembers can select a seat, regardless of fare type (rolls out with assigned seating system).1
  • Earlier Boarding: An "earlier boarding" benefit for cardmembers (details to come with assigned seating).1
  • First Checked Bag Free: Effective May 28, 2025, for the cardmember and up to eight companions on the same reservation.1

These new perks are in addition to existing benefits like anniversary points, points earning on purchases, EarlyBird Check-In®, Upgraded Boardings, travel credits (Priority card), and inflight purchase rebates (benefits vary by card).17 The new benefits, particularly the free checked bag, directly offset some of the new fare restrictions, making card ownership more valuable.

A-List Status: Upgraded Benefits for Loyal Flyers

Southwest’s A-List and A-List Preferred members will also see benefit enhancements:

A-List Members:

  • Checked Bags: First checked bag free (for member and up to eight companions) starting May 28, 2025.5
  • Seat Selection: Ability to select a Preferred or Standard seat at booking; option for Extra Legroom seat within 48 hours of departure (if available, no extra cost) – coming with assigned seating.5
  • Same-Day Standby: Remains a perk, even on Basic fares.13
  • Same-Day Change: Now requires purchase of a Choice, Choice Preferred, or Choice Extra fare.13
  • Existing perks like priority boarding and earning bonus continue.5

A-List Preferred Members:

  • Checked Bags: First and second checked bags free (for member and up to eight companions) starting May 28, 2025.5
  • Seat Selection: Select any available seat at booking, including Extra Legroom (if available, no extra cost) – coming with assigned seating.5
  • Same-Day Standby: Remains a perk, even on Basic fares.13
  • Same-Day Change: Also now requires purchase of a Choice, Choice Preferred, or Choice Extra fare.13
  • Existing perks like higher priority boarding, larger earning bonus, free inflight internet, and complimentary premium drinks continue.5

Other Notable Southwest Enhancements

Beyond fares and loyalty, Southwest is investing in the overall travel experience:

  • Assigned Seating: Coming in Q3 2025 for flights in 2026, with Standard, Preferred, and Extra Legroom seat options.1
  • Redeye Flights: Already introduced on some routes, with more planned.21
  • Cabin Upgrades: In-seat power, larger overhead bins, and faster WiFi are being rolled out.21
  • Digital Tools: Improved app features for baggage tracking, upgraded boarding purchases, and lap child management.21
  • Cash + Points: Book flights using a mix of points and cash; earn points on the cash portion for flights from January 1, 2025.14

Tips for Navigating the New Southwest

  • Choose Fares Wisely: Don't default to Basic. Assess if the restrictions on bags, seats, and changes are worth the lower price.
  • Maximize Credit Card Benefits: If you have a Southwest card, use the new free bag, seat selection, and boarding perks. Consider getting one if you fly Southwest regularly.
  • A-List Members, Adapt: Note the new same-day change rules; standby is still an option on Basic fares.
  • Book Before May 28, 2025 (for old rules): For travel where you want the old bag and flight credit rules, book before this date, but be aware that cancelling a pre-May 28 booking after May 28 may subject the credit to new expiration rules.8
  • Understand Flight Credit Expirations: Be mindful of the new 6-month (Basic) or 12-month (other fares) expiration for credits from post-May 28 bookings.8

Southwest is evolving to offer more customized experiences. While this means more complexity, understanding the new fare system and leveraging loyalty and credit card benefits will be key for travelers to continue finding value with the airline.1

title: Emirates Shakes Up Luxury Travel: Coveted First Class Awards Now an Elite-Only Perk – What US Flyers Need to Know
imageAlt: Interior view of an Emirates A380 First Class suite
author: News Contributor
snippet: Emirates has restricted its First Class 'Classic Rewards' to Skywards Platinum, Gold, or Silver elites, significantly impacting US travelers who often used transferred points for these aspirational flights.
content:
I. The End of an Era for Some? Emirates Restricts Iconic First Class Awards

The dream of flying Emirates First Class with Skywards miles is now tougher. Effective May 12, 2025, Emirates limited its First Class "Classic Rewards" to Skywards Platinum, Gold, or Silver elites.1 General Skywards Blue members, including those transferring points from US credit card programs, can no longer directly redeem for these seats.1 The change was quietly posted on Emirates' website with minimal notice—reportedly 36-48 hours—leaving non-elites little time to book.2 This caused disappointment among frequent flyers, as a popular path to ultra-luxury travel closed for many US travelers.3 The move reflects a trend of reserving premium experiences for highly engaged flyers.1

Table 1: Emirates First Class Award Changes – Key Facts

FeatureDetail
What's NewFirst Class "Classic Rewards" restricted to Skywards elite members.
Effective DateMay 12, 2025
Who's Affected (Skywards Direct Bookings)Skywards Blue (entry-level) members.
Who Can Still Book Directly (Skywards)Skywards Platinum, Gold, and Silver members.

II. Why the Change? Emirates' Stated Rationale and the Broader Industry Context

Emirates claims the change provides "premium and loyal members with more rewards...and greater access" to First Class.5 Analysts see it as managing high demand by prioritizing elites.8 Beyond this, it enhances exclusivity and may free seats for cash fares, continuing Emirates' trend of tightening First Class access.1 While other airlines like Air France and SWISS have similar policies, Emirates’ larger First Class footprint makes this more impactful.2 It questions the definition of "loyalty," potentially favoring direct flight activity over broader engagement like point transfers.1

III. The Ripple Effect: How This Impacts US Travelers

For US flyers, the impact is notable. Many accessed Emirates First Class by transferring points from programs like Amex, Chase, Citi, Capital One, and Bilt.1 This route is now largely closed to non-elites.3 Compounding this, Amex and Chase will temporarily pause Skywards transfers from May 29, 2025, and Citi's ratio worsens July 27, 2025.1 This reinforces the "earn and burn" philosophy: use miles promptly.2 The change elevates the importance of partner programs like Qantas and Aeroplan for accessing Emirates First Class, potentially shifting US travelers' points strategies, especially for popular fifth-freedom routes.2

IV. Navigating the New Landscape: Your Pathways to the Emirates First Class Suite

Despite hurdles, US travelers have options for Emirates First Class.

A. Partner Bookings: Restrictions don't affect partner bookings.5

  • Qantas Frequent Flyer: Still allows Emirates First Class bookings.5 US routes: New York (JFK)-Milan (MXP) for ~107,700 points + ~$100; Newark (EWR)-Athens (ATH) for ~129,300 points + ~$101.50.9 US-Dubai routes: ~150,000 points + >$800 surcharges.9 Qantas partners with Amex, Citi, Capital One.9
  • Air Canada Aeroplan: Retains access, but rates are often very high.2 Toronto-Dubai: 426,800 points + $118 CAD.2 Long-haul first can exceed 225,000 points.10 Aeroplan partners with Amex, Chase, Capital One, Bilt.2

Table 2: Booking Emirates First Class via Partners (Examples for US Travelers)

Partner ProgramExample US RouteApprox. MilesApprox. Fees & SurchargesKey Considerations
Qantas Frequent FlyerJFK-MXP107,700 QF~$100Good for US-Europe routes; lower surcharges than to DXB.
Qantas Frequent FlyerEWR-ATH129,300 QF~$101.50Good for US-Europe routes; lower surcharges than to DXB.
Qantas Frequent FlyerJFK-DXB~150,000 QF~$800+High surcharges to Dubai.
Air Canada AeroplanJFK-DXBVery High (e.g., 225k-475k+ AP)Varies, can be lower than QF to DXBExpect significantly more miles; check surcharges carefully.

B. Upgrade Strategy: Upgrading from Business to First with Skywards miles seems unaffected for non-elites, possible at airport/onboard, subject to availability.1

JFK-Dubai upgrade: ~70,200 miles; JFK-Milan/EWR-Athens: ~39,000 miles.10 Requires a Business Class ticket.4

C. Earning Skywards Elite Status: US co-branded Barclays cards offer a path:

  • Emirates Skywards Rewards World Elite MasterCard ($99 fee): Skywards Silver (1st year); retain with $20k annual spend.3
  • Emirates Skywards Premium World Elite MasterCard ($499 fee): Skywards Gold (1st year); retain with $40k annual spend.2

Silver status unlocks direct First Class awards.1 Flying also earns status.3

Table 3: Gaining Skywards Elite Status – US Credit Card Options

Emirates Skywards Rewards World Elite MC$99Silver$20,000 (for Silver)Unlocks direct First Class award bookings with Skywards.
Emirates Skywards Premium World Elite MC$499Gold$40,000 (for Gold)Unlocks direct First Class award bookings with Skywards.

V. Beyond Emirates: Exploring Alternative First Class Splurges for US Travelers

US travelers can explore other First Class products:

  • Etihad First Class Apartment (A380): Spacious suites, shower. JFK-Abu Dhabi. Book with AAdvantage or Etihad Guest miles (Amex, Capital One, Citi partner).14
  • Air France La Première: Exclusive, chic suites. JFK/LAX-Paris. Awards are very difficult, usually need Flying Blue Platinum status.15
  • Singapore Airlines Suites (A380): Large suites, top service. JFK-Frankfurt-Singapore. Book with KrisFlyer miles (transfers from major US bank programs).17
  • ANA "The Suite" (Boeing 777): Private suites, Japanese hospitality. JFK/ORD/SFO-Tokyo. Book with ANA Mileage Club (good value via Virgin Atlantic) or Star Alliance partners.19
  • Lufthansa First Class: Excellent ground service. Numerous US routes. Partner awards (Aeroplan, LifeMiles) usually open only within 14 days pre-departure.21

VI. Expert Take: The Golden Rules of Miles and Points in a Dynamic World

The Emirates restriction underscores key miles and points principles:

  • "Earn and Burn": Hoarding miles is risky due to devaluations and rule changes.2 Redeem for good value promptly.
  • Stay Informed and Flexible: Loyalty program news is vital. Flexibility in travel and redemption goals is key.
  • Value of Transferable Currencies: Bank points (Amex, Chase, etc.) offer protection against airline-specific devaluations, allowing pivots to other partners. Sudden changes can erode trust, potentially leading to strategic engagement with multiple programs.[ ]

VII. What's Next for Aspirational Awards? A Glimpse into the Future

Emirates' move may signal broader shifts. More airlines might gate exclusive products behind elite status or higher costs. A split could emerge: accessible economy/premium economy awards versus controlled ultra-premium First Class. Airlines use data analytics for loyalty program management and revenue.4 These changes are often data-driven, aiming for profitability and enhanced elite experiences. Despite challenges, savvy US travelers with knowledge, flexibility, and diversified points strategies can still achieve luxury flights. The game evolves, but enthusiasts adapt.

content:
Unlock More Travel: Top Credit Card Transfer Bonuses for US Travelers (May-June 2025 & Beyond)

Published: May 19, 2025

For savvy US travelers, credit card rewards are a cornerstone of funding adventures, and among the most powerful tools are transfer bonuses. These limited-time offers can significantly amplify the value of the points you earn, turning everyday spending into extraordinary travel experiences. If you're looking to make your points go further, understanding and strategically using these bonuses is key.

What Are Credit Card Transfer Bonuses?

Many leading travel rewards credit cards—from programs like American Express Membership Rewards, Chase Ultimate Rewards, Citi ThankYou Points, Capital One Miles, and Bilt Rewards—allow you to earn flexible points. Typically, these points can be transferred to airline and hotel loyalty programs, often at a 1:1 ratio.

A transfer bonus is a special promotion where your credit card issuer, in partnership with an airline or hotel, gives you extra points or miles when you make a transfer. For instance, a 25% transfer bonus means transferring 100,000 credit card points would net you 125,000 airline miles. This effectively lowers the points cost for your dream flight or hotel stay. These bonuses usually range from 10% to 50% (sometimes higher) but are always time-sensitive, often lasting about a month.

Why Transfer Bonuses Are a Game-Changer

Transfer bonuses allow you to extract significantly more value from your points. This could mean flying business class for the points cost of economy, adding extra nights to your vacation, or covering travel for more family members. They can make aspirational travel, like first-class suites or luxury resorts, more attainable.

Consider this: if you earned 2 points per dollar on dining, a 25% transfer bonus effectively boosts your earnings on that spend to 2.5 points per dollar when redeemed with the bonus. This highlights the power of transferable points, an advantage rarely seen with co-branded airline or hotel points. However, these deals don't last forever, so acting decisively is crucial.

Hottest Transfer Bonuses for May-June 2025 & Key Updates

Here’s a rundown of notable transfer bonuses and important program news relevant to US travelers. (Always confirm details and availability before transferring points.)

In-Depth Look at Current Opportunities:

  • Chase Ultimate Rewards:
    • Virgin Atlantic Flying Club (25% Bonus, ends June 15, 2025): Makes redemptions like ANA business class to Japan (from 52,500 Virgin points, so 42,000 Chase points) even more attractive.
    • Air France/KLM Flying Blue (25% Bonus, ends May 31, 2025): A prime candidate for SkyTeam flights to Europe. Combine this with Flying Blue’s "Promo Rewards" (often 25-50% off select routes) for potentially huge savings. For example, a 25,000-mile Promo Reward flight could become just 15,000 Chase points.
  • Citi ThankYou Points:
    • Qatar Airways Privilege Club (30% Bonus, ends May 31, 2025): Use 1,000 ThankYou points to get 1,300 Qatar Avios. Ideal for booking Qatar’s Qsuite. Note: bonus Avios may post up to a month after the base transfer.
    • Wyndham Rewards (25% Bonus, ends June 21, 2025): Transfer 1,000 ThankYou points for 1,250 Wyndham points. This is especially valuable for Vacasa vacation rentals (15,000 points/bedroom/night, so 12,000 Citi points with the bonus) and Wyndham’s fixed-tier hotels.
  • Capital One Miles:
    • Qantas Frequent Flyer (20% Bonus, ends May 31, 2025): Convert 1,000 Capital One miles to 1,200 Qantas points. Useful for Oneworld partner flights, like short-haul American Airlines flights (e.g., an 8,000 Qantas point flight becomes ~6,700 Capital One miles). Act before Qantas adjusts its award chart on August 5, 2025.
  • American Express Membership Rewards: Important Updates
    • No Widespread Bonuses Currently: Amex isn't offering public transfer bonuses right now, but always check your account for targeted promotions.
    • CRITICAL: Amex-to-Alaska via Hawaiian Airlines Ends June 30, 2025! The popular method of transferring Amex points to Alaska Airlines Mileage Plan via Hawaiian Airlines (1:1 from Hawaiian to Alaska) is being discontinued due to the Alaska-Hawaiian merger. If you plan to use Amex points for Alaska awards (known for great partner redemptions like JAL to Asia), make these transfers before this loophole closes.
    • Emirates Skywards Transfers Temporarily Unavailable (From May 28, 2025): Transfers to Emirates Skywards are paused. Monitor Emirates.com for updates.
  • Bilt Rewards: The "Rent Day" Special
    • Bilt offers unique, often high-value, transfer bonuses on the first of each month ("Rent Day"). For example, May 1st, 2025, featured a tiered bonus (25-100%) to Southwest Rapid Rewards (now expired). Bilt members should check their app monthly for new deals.

Smart Strategies to Maximize Transfer Bonuses

  • Have a Specific Redemption Ready: Only transfer points when you have a flight or hotel stay in mind and have confirmed award availability and cost. Transfers are generally irreversible.
  • Look for "Sweet Spots" & Stack Deals: Combine transfer bonuses with airline/hotel sales (like Flying Blue Promo Rewards) or program sweet spots (like Wyndham points for Vacasa rentals) for maximum impact.
  • Calculate, Don't Over-Transfer: Divide the points needed for redemption by (1 + Transfer Bonus Percentage) to find the credit card points to transfer. E.g., for a 100,000-mile award with a 25% bonus: 100,000 ÷ 1.25 = 80,000 credit card points.
  • Diversify Your Points (Strategically): Holding points in a couple of different transferable currencies (Amex, Chase, Citi, Capital One) offers flexibility to use the best bonus for your needs.

Common Pitfalls to Avoid

  • Speculative Transfers: Avoid transferring points hoping for a future use unless you're an advanced user who understands the risks (devaluation, availability changes).
  • Irreversibility: Once transferred, points usually can't be moved back.
  • Partner Program Expiration Policies: Your points will be subject to the airline or hotel program's expiration rules. Note these.
  • Transfer Times: While many are instant, some transfers take hours or days. The bonus portion (like with the current Citi to Qatar offer) can sometimes take even longer. Factor this into your booking plans.

Real Traveler Wins: The Power of Bonuses

  • Business Class to Europe: Travelers have used Amex bonuses to Virgin Atlantic to fly Air France Business Class for as few as 37,500 points. Stacking Chase bonuses with Flying Blue Promo Rewards can mean Europe for ~15,000 Chase points.
  • Affordable Domestic Flights: The Capital One to Qantas bonus can make short American Airlines flights cost around 6,700 Capital One miles.
  • Dream Vacation Rentals: A Vacasa rental, effectively costing 12,000 Citi points per night with the Wyndham bonus, can offer incredible value for family trips.

Your Next Adventure Awaits

The current landscape offers compelling opportunities, especially the Chase bonuses to Virgin Atlantic (June 15) and Flying Blue (May 31), Citi's offers to Qatar Airways (May 31) and Wyndham (June 21), and Capital One's Qantas bonus (May 31). And crucially for Amex cardholders, remember the June 30, 2025, deadline for the Amex-to-Hawaiian-to-Alaska transfer.

Review your points balances and travel goals. By being strategic, informed, and acting promptly, these transfer bonuses can unlock remarkable travel value, stretching your hard-earned rewards further than ever. Stay engaged with loyalty program news to catch the next great deal!
